bullets.title: Anthropic S-1 alleviates AI buildout fears; $750B+ compute commitments underpin hyperscaler capex
bullets.body: Anthropic's S-1 disclosed H1'26 revenue of $16.3B (+1,400% YoY), 11,900+ enterprise customers with $100K+ spend, and NRR of ~900%. The filing revealed $110B committed to AMZN through 2036, $114.5B to GOOGL through 2033, plus $161.2B to Broadcom and $120.5B to SpaceX.AI — alleviating broad AI buildout concerns and driving bullish reads for compute infrastructure (CRWV, NBIS) and software. Customer concentration falling sharply: top-5 share dropped from ~36% of Q1'26 to ~21% of Q3'26 revenue.

bullets.title: AVGO arranges $63B chip-financing facility for Anthropic with $45B residual value guarantee
bullets.body: Broadcom structured a $63B financing vehicle for Anthropic's CY27 chip purchases, providing a residual value support (RSV) backstop on $45B — bringing AVGO's total RSV exposure to $74B including a June tranche for CY26. Analysts read this as confirmation that AI compute spending in CY27/28 is highly likely to occur and that residual-value guarantees are becoming standard deal structure for hyperscaler chip financing.

bullets.title: META prices $35B equity raise; funding covers ~half of $180-220B capex need through 2028
bullets.body: META priced a 40M-share secondary at $625 and a $12.5B mandatory convertible preferred, with up to $60B Class C ATM planned for 1Q27+. Hedgeye estimates the full $95B equity package covers ~half the $180-220B total funding need on a $500B capex assumption; without financing, cash would run out by 3Q27. AMD invested $1B in the equity offering as part of a strategic AI infrastructure partnership.

bullets.title: Global data center capacity shortfall of 49 GW by 2028 makes EQIX MS top pick
bullets.body: Morgan Stanley's Cameron McVeigh model projects global DC IT capacity of 316GW by 2030 (>20% CAGR) with a 49GW supply shortfall by 2028 (43GW US-only). EQIX named MS top pick for colocation advantage; colocation providers expected to lose only ~3 percentage points of market share to hyperscalers by 2030. Data center power demand is driving utility capex upgrades — CNP raised its 10-year capex plan by $4B to $70.7B.

bullets.title: McCullough bearish equities: S&P forming lower highs, VIX breaking out, 10Y at 5.10%
bullets.body: Hedgeye's McCullough flagged the S&P 500 forming lower highs, Nasdaq and Russell 2000 with bearish TREND signals, and VIX breaking out with range bottom rising into the 16s from 10-12. The 10-year yield broke TRADE at 5.10% and the 30-year broke both TRADE and TREND; Brent crude signaling toward $120, reinforcing stagflation in what he frames as a Quad 3 environment. He is shorting META and GOOGL on bounces and sold all Bitcoin.

bullets.title: Internet sector down 4% in 3Q earnings season; mega-caps at 19-21x '27 EPS with meaningful multiple compression
bullets.body: Internet names fell 4% while SPX was flat and NDX down 1% during the 3Q earnings window. META dropped 9%, GOOGL 6%; AMZN/GOOGL/META now trade at 19-21x '27 EPS with EPS multiples down 18%/14%/2% versus TTM average. Morgan Stanley maintains an Attractive industry view despite the de-rating.

bullets.title: Tech shorts covering aggressively; short volume 19% below average — lowest in 4 weeks
bullets.body: Citi notes shorts covering across tech at the fastest pace in a month, with short volume 19% below average, making tech the most-covered sector. Buy-side expects MSFT Azure +47%+ cc in F1Q with F2Q guided similarly; GOOGL buyside models 3Q Search ~14.5%, Cloud +100%+; AMZN buyside models AWS ~43% with OI in the high-30s to low-40s.

bullets.title: MSFT F1Q27 preview: Azure +44.3% consensus, $50B+ quarterly capex, 60K voluntary buyout program in focus
bullets.body: Street consensus for MSFT F1Q27 is $90.6B revenue with Azure +44.3% YoY; buy-side estimates are likely higher. Management guided F1Q27 capex over $50B with FY26 capex at $175B. The 60K voluntary buyout (27% of workforce) is viewed as a margin-preservation move as AI capex pressure mounts; Nadella separately flagged inference demand running materially stronger than expected.

bullets.title: MS 3Q GDP tracking raised to 3.2%; durable goods beat but housing stuck with prices accelerating
bullets.body: Morgan Stanley raised 3Q GDP tracking to 3.2% from 3.1% after September durable goods orders rose 1.8% m/m and inventory investment came in stronger than expected, offsetting slightly softer equipment spending (now tracking 13% annualized vs 15% prior). September new home sales fell 0.6% m/m to 676K with 3Q real residential investment tracking at -3.9% q/q, while Case-Shiller home prices accelerated to +2.09% YoY.

bullets.title: ADP private payrolls slowing: 4-week average hiring at 16.75K, second consecutive week of deceleration
bullets.body: UBS flagged ADP's 4-week average private payroll additions slowed to 16.75K from 17.5K the prior week, the second consecutive week of deceleration. The ADP survey covers approximately 26M private workers and excludes federal employees.

bullets.title: Market correlation at historical 0.4th percentile — extreme fragmentation favors stock selection over factor bets
bullets.body: Six-month stock correlations collapsed to the 0.4th historical percentile, signaling extreme market fragmentation. Tech and hyperscalers represent 46% of S&P 500 weight, heavily influencing headline returns; since the Oct 6 peak, most sectors gained on an equal-weighted basis while Tech and Communications underperformed. Quant strategists recommend long Freight/short Airlines in Transportation and Cash Return selection within Banks.

bullets.title: Hedgeye rotates: sells Bitcoin/gold/silver, buys yen/healthcare/staples ETFs on rising stagflation risk
bullets.body: McCullough sold all IBIT (Bitcoin) positions and exited gold, silver, and corn longs; silver and palladium moved to outright shorts. He bought 50bps each in FXY (yen), XLV (healthcare), and XLP (staples), while selling PFIX and DBMF. Bitcoin TREND level cited at $79,000 — a break would trigger further sales. Healthcare and software remain sources of long performance.

bullets.title: AI sector at July lows amid rotation; Raymond James hosting 10/30 call to assess valuation reset and hyperscaler spending
bullets.body: Raymond James flagged the AI market at July lows as sector rotation weighs, while the non-AI market is improving as rates decline. The 10/30 call will cover hyperscaler earnings, AI economics, compute financing, memory pricing, and software disruption risks — including Amazon, CoreWeave, and SpaceX strategies.

bullets.title: Semiconductor fundamentals strong but SOX testing 200-DMA; DRAM pricing positive through 1H28
bullets.body: Goldman Sachs flags semiconductor capex and EPS estimates rising with valuations at ~1x discount to the 15-year average, but the SOX Index is testing its 200-day moving average for the first time since June 2025. TrendForce sees no meaningful DRAM capacity additions before 2028; pricing outlook is positive throughout 2027 and into 1H28.

bullets.title: Geopolitical wildcard: Netanyahu election loss would reduce oil risk premia; GCC-Iran deal pathway opens
bullets.body: 22V Research notes that if Netanyahu loses the Israeli election, oil market risk premia would decline materially as the principal pro-escalation leader exits. IDF Chief of Staff publicly accused Netanyahu of pushing an Iran conflict for electoral purposes two days before the election. GCC-led diplomacy toward a US-Iran deal is seen as more viable under a different Israeli government.

bullets.title: Eurozone credit tightening further; bank lending standards tighten on geopolitical risk, demand weakens
bullets.body: ECB surveys show annual bank lending grew 3.6% YoY in September but financing conditions tightened for firms and consumer credit. Loan demand weakened for both households and firms on higher borrowing costs and lower confidence; expected selling-price growth jumped to 3.6% from 2.5%. The data does not yet capture the acute October rise in French yields or recent political tensions.

bullets.title: FTNT F3Q26 earnings preview: slight beat expected on revenue, margins, EPS; FY27 outlook the key watch item
bullets.body: Street expects Fortinet to report F3Q26 revenue of $2.064B (vs $2.055B guidance midpoint), gross margin of 80.1%, operating margin of 36.2%, and EPS of $0.86 — all modestly above guidance. Investor focus is on product vs service revenue mix, SASE/Firewall momentum, AI Infrastructure & OT security, and FY27 demand durability commentary.

bullets.title: Pre-market: S&P futures +0.37%; AVGO +3.3%, RCL +5.3%, AFRM +2.7%; 10Y at 4.99%
bullets.body: S&P futures rose 28 points (+0.37%) to 7,742. Key movers: AVGO +3.3% on the $63B Anthropic financing deal and a DA Davidson upgrade; RCL +5.3% on its Q3 beat and guidance raise (CCL +2.4% in sympathy); AFRM +2.7% in sympathy with SoFi (+11.4%). HUBS fell 3.4% on a UBS downgrade and ADBE slid 1.4%. The 10-year yield was +1bp to 4.99%.

bullets.title: Redbook retail sales +9.3% YoY, accelerating sequentially; 2-year comp +7.3%
bullets.body: Redbook retail sales data for the latest week showed +9.3% YoY growth, accelerating sequentially with a 2-year comp of +7.3%. Home improvement retail sales also accelerated to +2.7% in September from +0.8% in June, though LIRA projects homeowner spending growth slowing to +0.5-0.6% by 1Q-2Q27.

bullets.title: ServiceNow Q3 preview: $4.09B revenue, 10.2% options-implied move; AI ACV monetization and cRPO deceleration in focus
bullets.body: Street consensus for NOW Q3 is $4.09B revenue and $1.02 EPS with cRPO guidance of +19.5% YoY and operating margin ~31%. NOW is up 65.7% since late July vs S&P +2.4%; bulls cite AI ACV momentum and Federal deals while bears flag organic cRPO deceleration and Microsoft/AI-native competition. Options imply a ~10.2% move.
